label: <DEL> step when the first original token is c/q/n/f/w/l/s
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (93% of activation mass; 11% of all <DEL> steps are active). The output at that step is original token 0, and that token strongly modulates firing: c (strongest, about 10x lift), then q, n, f, w, l, s. Top activations are all <DEL> steps with first token c. Rarely fires in the original phase (about 7% of mass, weak, mostly on g/p/i/j inputs at t = 3-6) and almost never in the copy phase. Also stronger on shorter sequences (L = 4-5) and when the next output (orig(1)) is in the same letter set, but adding either condition did not cleanly improve the fit. The predicate gets most of the mass (dev mass recall 0.88), but precision is only about 0.42: many <DEL> steps with these first tokens stay below threshold, especially in long sequences.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: c, q, f, n, w, s; least: g, m, t, u) and the next token to output (most: f, s, n, l, q, c; least: o, i, g, p); timing cues that raise it most: t=4, t=3, t=5.
